mainEntity.name: How much does a Peugeot 2008 1.2 PureTech engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Peugeot 2008 1.2 PureTech engine typically costs £1,200-£2,100 supply-only, depending on power output and condition. EB2 100hp units start around £1,200, while EB2DT 130hp turbo units range £1,400-£2,100. Used engines start from £500. Supply & fit adds £400-£800 labour. Peugeot dealer replacement can exceed £6,000.

mainEntity.name: What causes the Peugeot 2008 1.2 PureTech low oil pressure warning?

acceptedAnswer.text: The low oil pressure warning on Peugeot 2008 1.2 PureTech engines is caused by wet timing belt degradation. The belt sheds rubber particles into the engine oil, which block the oil pump strainer and starve the engine of lubrication. Peugeot recommends belt inspection every 20,000 km or 1 year, with belt width measurement (<16.6mm).

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a Peugeot 2008 1.2 PureTech?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a Peugeot 2008 1.2 PureTech engine is usually worthwhile if the vehicle is otherwise sound. A rebuilt unit costs £1,200-£2,100 versus £4,000-£16,000 for a comparable used 2008. With Peugeot dealer replacement exceeding £6,000, specialist rebuilt units offer exceptional value.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Peugeot 2008 1.2 PureTech engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance, Peugeot 2008 1.2 PureTech engines typically reach 100,000-150,000 miles. However, the wet belt is the critical lifespan limiter - Peugeot recommends replacement at 60,000 miles or 6 years, whichever comes first. Regular oil changes with correct PSA-approved oil and belt inspections are essential for longevity.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between EB2, EB2DT and EB2ADT engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The EB2 family powers all Peugeot 2008 1.2 PureTech variants. EB2 is the 100hp naturally aspirated unit. EB2ADT is the 110hp turbocharged mid-range option. EB2DT is the 130hp turbocharged high-output unit fitted to GT and GT Premium trims. All share the same wet belt vulnerability.

mainEntity.name: How do I find my Peugeot 2008 1.2 PureTech engine code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your Peugeot 2008 1.2 PureTech engine code appears on the VIN plate under the bonnet, stamped on the engine block, or on your V5C registration document section D.2. Common codes include EB2 (100hp), EB2DT (130hp turbo), EB2ADT (110hp turbo) and EB2F (82hp VTi). Enter your reg above for instant verification.

historyTimeline.h2: Peugeot 2008 1.2 PureTech - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Peugeot 2008 1.2 PureTech has been the dominant petrol engine across both generations of the compact crossover - the first-generation A94 (2013-2019) and the second-generation P24 (2019-present). Part of PSA's EB2 family, the 1.2 PureTech replaced earlier VTi units with a more efficient three-cylinder design, offering outputs from 82hp to 130hp across Active, Allure and GT trims. However, the engine's wet timing belt design has made it the subject of intense UK replacement demand.

milestones.description: **2013** - Peugeot 2008 launched with EB2F 1.2L VTi 82hp (naturally aspirated) and EB2 1.2L PureTech 100hp
**2014** - PureTech 1.2L becomes the primary petrol engine across the range
**2015** - EB2DT 1.2L PureTech 130hp turbo introduced for GT and higher-spec trims
**2016** - EB2ADT 1.2L PureTech 110hp added as mid-range option
**2019** - Second-generation (P24) 2008 debuts with revised EB2ADT and EB2DT units
**2021** - Peugeot issues technical bulletin on PureTech belt inspection and revised maintenance intervals
**2024** - Stellantis launches Customer Support Programme covering wet belt and oil pressure issues for up to 10 years / 112,000 miles

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every EB2 engine fitted to the Peugeot 2008 1.2 PureTech is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Peugeot 2008 1.2 PureTech Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Peugeot 2008 1.2 PureTech's EB2 engine family is the subject of intense UK replacement demand due to one critical vulnerability - the wet timing belt. Unlike conventional belts, the PureTech's belt runs inside the engine, constantly exposed to heat and engine oil. Over time, the belt degrades, shedding rubber particles that clog the oil pump strainer, triggering low oil pressure warnings and, if ignored, catastrophic engine failure. Every rebuilt Peugeot 2008 1.2 PureTech engine through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Wet Belt Failure - Why Peugeot 2008 1.2 PureTech Engines Lose Oil Pressure
problems.rootCause: The wet timing belt degrades over time, shedding rubber particles into the engine oil. These particles block the oil pump strainer, starving the engine of lubrication and triggering the low oil pressure warning. Peugeot recommends belt inspection every 20,000 km (12,000 miles) or annually, with replacement at 60,000 miles or 6 years.

repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early; prevents engine damage; average wet belt replacement £890

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full engine flush, oil pump replacement, belt change, new gaskets, strainer cleaning
repairOptions.longevity: May restore function if no bearing damage occurred

repairOptions.longevity: Only option once bearings or crankshaft are damaged

A preventative belt change at a specialist is far cheaper than a full replacement - typically £900-£1,400 versus £1,200-£2,100 for a rebuilt engine. Peugeot recommends belt replacement at 60,000 miles or 6 years. Once the engine has seized or knocked, only a rebuilt unit makes financial sense.

problems.rootCause: Belt debris blocks the oil pump pickup strainer, starving the engine of lubrication and triggering the dashboard warning. The warning may appear intermittently at first, often flashing briefly then disappearing.

problems.h4: Turbocharger & High-Pressure Fuel Pump Failure - EB2DT Specific Issues
problems.rootCause: The turbocharged EB2DT unit places additional stress on the wet belt system and high-pressure fuel pump. Belt debris can starve the turbo of oil, while HPFP wear causes hard starting and loss of power.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New turbocharger, high-pressure fuel pump, oil feed lines, system flush
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before engine damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with upgraded turbo, HPFP and wet belt system
repairOptions.longevity: Required if turbo failure has caused engine damage

problems.recommendation: If your Peugeot 2008 1.2 PureTech 130 has turbo or HPFP issues alongside wet belt degradation, a full rebuilt engine is the most reliable long-term solution. Replacing individual components on a contaminated engine risks repeat failures.
